report:
Brain, fourth ventricular tumour

Received in formalin is an intact tumour mass from the fourth ventricle, measuring 45 x 35 x 20 mm in aggregate. The cut surface is soft and grey-tan with areas of haemorrhage and yellow necrosis. Representative sections are taken; see block key.

(A1-A6) tumour.

Specimen
- Procedure: Suboccipital craniectomy and excision
- Tumour site: Fourth ventricle
- Extent of resection as stated by the surgeon: Gross total resection
- Specimen integrity: Single intact mass

Microscopic findings
- Tumour histology:
  Sections show a glial neoplasm forming perivascular pseudorosettes, the cells having monomorphic round nuclei and fibrillary processes radiating on to the vessel walls. The tumour shows true ependymal rosettes and increased cellularity. Mitoses number 2 per 10 high-power fields. The adjacent brain parenchyma shows reactive gliosis. On immunohistochemistry, the tumour cells are positive for GFAP, with EMA positive with dot-like staining and H3 K27 trimethylation shows loss of nuclear expression. The Ki-67 proliferation index is approximately 8 per cent. On molecular testing, methylation profiling assigns the tumour to the posterior fossa group A class.
- Treatment effect: No known presurgical therapy

Integrated diagnosis
- Integrated diagnosis: Posterior fossa ependymoma, group PFA, CNS WHO grade 2
- Histopathological classification: Ependymoma
- CNS WHO grade: 2

Molecular information
- Other molecular studies: Methylation profiling assigns the tumour to the
  posterior fossa group A class

Additional findings
- Adjacent brain parenchyma with reactive gliosis

BRAIN, fourth ventricle, suboccipital craniectomy and excision
- POSTERIOR FOSSA EPENDYMOMA, group PFA, CNS WHO grade 2; see synoptic report
